establishes: The Internet Foundation existed as a non-governmental organization by at least 2013.
The Internet Foundation was seeking the creation of a universal declaration of digital rights.
IAPP had covered that effort as far back as 2013.
Dele Atanda and the Internet Foundation had proposed ethical-data-use standards work to BSI before the 2017 article.
That work concerned ethical definitions and standards for privacy, ownership, consent, fair use, data transfer, correction, erasure, arbitration, and notification.
The initiative was connected to standards work beyond baseline legal compliance, including GDPR and the changing UK data-protection environment.
